cfbl-institute-policies.text:
CFBL Institute Continuing Education Policies
These policies apply to all CFBL Institute live continuing education programs. Questions, requests, and grievances go to the ACEP Administrator at drserravalle@gmail.com or (302) 608-3780.
Program Fees, Refunds, and Cancellation
Fees.
 The fee for each program is published on its registration page before registration opens. Fees include live instruction, program materials, and a certificate of completion for verified attendance.
Refunds.
 A participant who cancels in writing at least 7 days before the program date receives a full refund. A participant who cancels fewer than 7 days before the program date may transfer once, at no charge, to a future offering of the same program, or receive a refund less a 10 percent administrative fee. No refund is issued after the program begins.
Requests.
 Refund and transfer requests are submitted in writing to the ACEP Administrator and processed within 14 business days.
Cancellation by CFBL Institute.
 If CFBL Institute cancels or reschedules a program, registered participants are notified in writing and offered a full refund or a transfer to a future offering at no additional cost. CFBL Institute is not responsible for other costs participants incur in anticipation of a canceled program.
Participant Complaints and Grievances
Participants may submit a written grievance about program content, instruction, accessibility, or administration to the ACEP Administrator at drserravalle@gmail.com. A grievance should identify the program and date, describe the concern, and state the resolution requested.
The ACEP Administrator acknowledges receipt in writing within 5 business days. The Program Administrator reviews the grievance and provides a written response within 14 business days of receipt describing the review, findings, and any action taken. A participant who is not satisfied with the resolution may contact NBCC at continuinged@nbcc.org. CFBL Institute does not retaliate against anyone who submits a grievance. Grievance records are retained for 5 years.
Confidentiality of Participant Information
CFBL Institute collects only the information needed to administer programs, meet recordkeeping requirements, and communicate with participants about programs and certificates. Payment card data is processed by Shopify and is not stored by CFBL Institute. Participant information is stored in access-restricted systems, is not sold or shared for marketing, and is not used outside program administration without consent. Participants may request a copy of, or a correction to, their information by emailing the ACEP Administrator.
Attendance and Certificates
Attendance at live programs is verified with the registration roster, the Zoom attendance report or sign-in sheet, and in-session check-ins. Credit is awarded for verified instructional time attended, in quarter-hour increments; breaks, meals, and introductions are not counted. Certificates are issued after the program ends and are emailed within 7 business days. Replacement certificates are available at no cost for 5 years.
Accessibility
CFBL Institute provides accessible programs consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Live Zoom sessions offer captioning. Participants may request accommodations at registration or at any time by contacting the ACEP Administrator; requests receive a response within 5 business days.

Film on Sunday, September 27
Film · 1 min 30 sec
Week 1 · September 27, 2026
Trauma and Recovery
Judith Herman, 1992
Why read it
Herman called stage one safety and stabilization. We have newer language for it now, but the clinical problem she identified has not changed. Stage one is not teaching coping skills so that we can get to the work. It is the work. Most stuck cases are stage one problems being treated as stage two.
Worth knowing
Many clients with complex histories can begin processing sooner than a strict phase model suggests (de Jongh et al., 2016).
Best for
Clinicians early in trauma work, and anyone whose cases keep stalling once processing begins.
Where its central claim sits
Established
Emerging
Theoretical
Clinical wisdom
Film on Sunday, October 4
Film · 1 min 33 sec
Week 2 · October 4, 2026
The Body Keeps the Score
Bessel van der Kolk, 2014
Why read it
It moved trauma beyond the idea that suffering lives only in thoughts and memories, and it made the body impossible to ignore. Still worth reading. Also worth arguing with.
Worth knowing
The body carries patterns rather than stored files, and those patterns look different in every client. The book draws on polyvagal theory, which research is still testing (Grossman, 2023).
Best for
Clinicians who need the body in the case conceptualization. Read it alongside a critique.
Where its central claim sits
Established
Emerging
Theoretical
Clinical wisdom
Film on Sunday, October 11
Film · 1 min 44 sec
Week 3 · October 11, 2026
Healing the Fragmented Selves of Trauma Survivors
Janina Fisher, 2017
Why read it
Internal contradiction is not necessarily resistance. Fisher gives clinicians a way to work with the client who wants treatment and dreads every session, without turning that into pathology or noncompliance. We stop trying to make one part win.
Worth knowing
Parts language is a useful clinical map. Research on the structure beneath it is still developing.
Best for
Clinicians whose clients seem to get in the way of their own treatment.
Where its central claim sits
Established
Emerging
Theoretical
Clinical wisdom
Film on Sunday, October 18
Film · 1 min 26 sec
Week 4 · October 18, 2026
Complex PTSD: From Surviving to Thriving
Pete Walker, 2013
Why read it
Some histories have no single event in the timeline. Walker gave us language for emotional flashbacks without a visual narrative: a client suddenly feels very young, ashamed, trapped or defective, and does not know why.
Worth knowing
Not every difficult childhood is a trauma diagnosis. Complex PTSD is recognized in ICD-11, and the fawn response is a newer idea that research is still catching up to.
Best for
Clinicians working with adults whose history is a developmental environment rather than an event. Readable for many clients as well.
Where its central claim sits
Established
Emerging
Theoretical
Clinical wisdom
Film on Sunday, October 25
Film · 33 sec
Week 5 · October 25, 2026
Radical Acceptance
Tara Brach, 2003
Why read it
Not a manual and not a modality. A way of meeting what is here without judgment, which is harder than it sounds and more useful in the room than most techniques. Read it, then practice it.
Worth knowing
It is a practice book rather than a treatment protocol, and its ideas share roots with acceptance-based therapies such as ACT and DBT.
Best for
Clinicians building their own capacity to stay present with what they cannot fix.
Where its central claim sits
Established

Theoretical
Clinical wisdom
Film on Sunday, November 1
Film · 31 sec
Week 6 · November 1, 2026
Mindset
Carol S. Dweck, 2006
Why read it
Not a treatment model. A way of thinking: the shift from a fixed to a growth mindset, and what changes when you apply it to business, sports, health care and relationships.
Worth knowing
Growth mindset research shows real but modest effects, strongest for students who are struggling (Sisk et al., 2018; Yeager et al., 2019).
Best for
Supervisors, educators, and clinicians who coach or teach.
Where its central claim sits
Established

Clinical wisdom
Every book is sorted by where its central claim sits: established, emerging, theoretical, or clinical wisdom. Clinical wisdom is not a dismissal. It is often right and simply has not been tested yet.

Meet the Trainer
Niki Serravalle, PsyD, LPCMH, NCC
Founded and led by Dr. Niki Serravalle, licensed clinical psychologist and founder of the Center for Balanced Living. CFBL Institute exists to bridge the gap between clinical theory and applied practice. Our work is grounded in trauma-informed science, nervous system awareness, cultural humility, and the lived complexity of real clinical work.
drserravalle@gmail.com
Full Bio
Training is how clinical knowledge moves from one clinician to the next. I teach because the best of what I learned came from clinicians who showed me how they thought, not just what to do. That is the kind of training I try to offer now.
Niki Serravalle, PsyD, LPCMH, NCC
FAQ
Registration
Everything to know before you register. Do not see your question here? Reach out and we will answer it.
Who are the trainings for?
Our trainings are built for licensed mental health clinicians, including psychologists, LCSWs, LPCs, LMFTs, LMHCs, PMHNPs, and MDs, as well as graduate students in clinical and counseling psychology. Each offering lists the clinical experience it assumes so you can choose the right fit.
What is the format?
Most trainings are delivered live online so you can attend from anywhere, with slides and handouts shared with registrants. Some run as a multi-session series with time to integrate between meetings. The length, schedule, and any pre-work are listed on each training's page.
How do I register, and what if a training is full?
Registration opens on each training's page once dates are confirmed. When a cohort is full or dates are still being scheduled, you can join the waitlist. Waitlist members hear first and are invited to register before seats open to the public.
Will I receive a certificate or continuing education credit?
Registrants receive a certificate of completion listing the training title, date, and hours attended. A certificate of completion is not continuing education credit. When a program carries CE credit, its page names the approving body. If you have a specific licensing-board requirement, reach out before registering.
What does it cost, and are group rates available?
Pricing is listed on each training's page and varies by length and format. Reduced student rates are available for many offerings, and we offer group rates for agencies or practices enrolling several clinicians. Contact us for a group quote.
What if I need to cancel or need an accommodation?
If you need to cancel, let us know as early as you can and we will arrange a transfer or a credit toward a future cohort. If you need an accommodation to take part fully, tell us when you register so we can plan ahead.

clinical-supervision.title: Clinical Supervision in Delaware | Center for Balanced Living
clinical-supervision.text:
Clinical Supervision
Supervision for clinicians working toward licensure
Individual supervision with Dr. Niki Serravalle, PsyD, LPCMH, NCC, for LPC associates and PsyD trainees accruing supervised hours in Delaware. Her doctoral training, LPCMH licensure, and more than 20 years of clinical experience meet the requirements to supervise toward both licenses.
The work centers on case conceptualization, diagnostic reasoning, and trauma-informed treatment planning, with the documentation your licensing board requires.
Ask About Openings
Meet Dr. Serravalle
Focus Areas
What Supervision Covers
Case Conceptualization
Formulations you can defend in a chart review or a staffing.
Diagnostic Reasoning
Differentials, thresholds, and rule-outs, worked through on your own cases.
Trauma-Informed Treatment
Sequencing, stabilization, and knowing when a client is ready for processing.
Assessment Literacy
Reading test data and reports, and translating them into treatment.
Ethics and Documentation
Notes, consent, boundaries, and the gray areas the licensure exam does not cover.
Licensure Logistics
Hour logs and board forms, completed accurately and on time.
How It Starts
Four Steps to Begin
1
Send a Note
Your license type, current setting, and the hours you still need.
2
Fit Conversation
A brief call about your caseload, goals, and schedule.
3
Written Agreement
Frequency, fees, and documentation, set out before you begin.
4
Regular Supervision
Scheduled sessions built around your actual cases.
Questions, Answered
Common Questions About Supervision
Who is supervision available for?
LPC associates and PsyD trainees accruing supervised hours toward licensure as mental health counselors or psychologists.
Is Dr. Serravalle qualified to supervise toward Delaware licensure?
Yes. Delaware does not certify supervisors separately. Supervisors qualify through their own credentials and experience, and Dr. Serravalle's PsyD, LPCMH licensure, and more than 20 years of clinical practice meet the requirements for supervising both LPC associates and PsyD trainees.
What does supervision focus on?
Case conceptualization, diagnostic reasoning, trauma-informed treatment planning, ethical decision making, and the documentation licensure requires. Sessions work from your actual caseload, so the skills transfer directly to your clients.
How are frequency and fees set?
Both are agreed in a written supervision agreement before you begin, along with how your hours will be documented.
How do I get started?
Send a message through the contact form or call (302) 608-3780. Include your license type, setting, and the hours you still need, and we will respond within 24 to 48 hours.
Take the Next Step
Ask about supervision openings
Tell us your license type, current setting, and how many hours you still need. We respond within 24 to 48 hours.

EMDR Consultation
Consultation toward EMDR certification
Dr. Niki Serravalle is a Certified EMDR Therapist, EMDRIA Approved Consultant, and EMDRIA approved trainer. Consultation is for clinicians who have completed an EMDRIA approved basic training and want to apply EMDR with more precision on real cases.
Individual and group consultation, online or in person in Townsend.
Book Individual Consultation
Join Group Consultation
Focus Areas
What Consultation Covers
Protocol Fidelity
Applying the eight phases and the standard protocol as designed.
Complex Presentations
Adapting EMDR for dissociation, attachment disruption, and complex trauma.
Toward Certification
Consultation hours documented for your EMDRIA certification application.
Case Review
Target selection, case conceptualization, and phase decisions on your own cases.
Preparation and Stabilization
Building the resources a client needs before processing begins.
Individual or Group
Choose the format that fits your hours and your caseload.
How It Works
From Registration to Certification
1
Register
Choose individual or group consultation and book it here on the site.
2
Bring a Case
Come with a case or a question about the protocol.
3
Work It Through
Conceptualization, target selection, and phase decisions, reviewed together.
4
Track Your Hours
Your hours are documented for your certification application.
Questions, Answered
Common Questions About EMDR Consultation
Do I need to complete EMDR basic training first?
Yes. Consultation is for therapists who have completed an EMDRIA approved basic training. It is the next step in the certification process and builds directly on that training.
What happens during consultation?
Case review, protocol refinement, and integrating EMDR with complex presentations, including dissociation, attachment disruption, and co-occurring conditions. The focus is fidelity to the Adaptive Information Processing model and the clinical reasoning that moves practice beyond technique.
How many consultation hours do I need for certification?
EMDRIA certification requires 10 hours of consultation with an EMDRIA Approved Consultant, in addition to the 10 hours completed during basic training. Dr. Serravalle documents your hours for your certification application.
Is consultation online or in person?
Both. Individual and group consultation are available online or in person in Townsend.
Take the Next Step

credentials.title: Clinical Credentials and Training | Center for Balanced Living
credentials.text:
Why Our Community Trust Us
Credentials
We believe healing happens in relationship, and that good care is built on a strong clinical foundation. Our work draws on advanced training in trauma treatment, psychological evaluation, and integrative care, so the support you receive is both clinically rigorous and attuned to who you are.
Center for Balanced Living provides trauma-informed therapy and psychological evaluation in Townsend, Delaware, and the surrounding Middletown area. This page outlines the clinical credentials and training behind our approach to assessment and treatment.
Where the training goes to work
Every certification on this page is put to use in the same place: our office in Townsend, where Dr. Serravalle sees clients, conducts evaluations, and consults with other clinicians.
At a Glance
Credentials & Certifications
Select an area to learn what it means for your care.
IFS
EMDR
TF-CBT
DBT
ACT
Ecotherapy
MBSR
Polyvagal
CPT
A compassionate way of understanding the different parts of ourselves, and helping them work together with less conflict.
Learn more
Certified EMDR Therapist & EMDRIA Approved Consultant
We are certified in EMDR and approved by EMDRIA to consult with other clinicians. EMDR helps the brain reprocess painful or stuck experiences, so trauma loses its grip and healing can move forward.
Learn more
Certified Trauma-Focused CBT Therapist
For children and teens carrying the weight of trauma, we use TF-CBT, a structured, evidence-based approach that gently reduces symptoms and helps young people, and their families, find steadier ground.
Learn more
Dialectical Behavior Therapy
When emotions feel overwhelming, DBT offers concrete skills, regulation, distress tolerance, mindfulness, and healthier connection, that make daily life more livable.
Learn more
Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
ACT helps when you feel stuck in avoidance or self-criticism. Together we build psychological flexibility and reconnect your daily choices with what matters most to you.
Learn more
Certified through the Earth Body Institute
Some of the most grounding work happens in connection with the natural world. Our ecotherapy training brings nature-based practices into care to support reflection, regulation, and a felt sense of calm.
Learn about ecotherapy
Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR)
MBSR training informs how we help clients notice inner experience, soften reactivity, and respond with more intention through present-moment practices.
Learn more
Polyvagal-Informed Therapy
Polyvagal-informed care attends to the nervous system's role in safety and connection, helping you understand your body's responses and build a felt sense of regulation and safety.
Learn more
Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT)
CPT is a structured, evidence-based therapy for PTSD that helps you examine and shift the stuck points trauma can leave in how you see yourself, others, and the world.
Learn more
Additional Training & Integrative Approaches
The deeper toolkit we draw from to meet each person where they are.
Emotional Freedom Technique (EFT)
A gentle, tapping-based approach used alongside therapy to ease emotional distress and support regulation.
Trauma-Conscious Yoga (TCY)
Trauma-sensitive, body-based practices that support nervous-system regulation and reconnection with the body.
Somatic Psychology (SP)
Mind-body awareness brought into treatment, with attention to the nervous system and the embodied experience of stress and trauma.
Breathwork
Structured breathing practices that support grounding, regulation, and emotional awareness in the work of healing and growth.
Narrative Therapy
Helps clients separate from the problem and re-author the story they live by, drawing on their values, strengths, and lived experience.
Art & Movement Therapies
Expression beyond words, using creativity and the body to support processing, regulation, and self-understanding.
Curious Whether We're the Right Fit?
Let's start a conversation
Tell us what you're looking for, and we'll help you find the right next step. We usually reach out within 24-48 hours.
Start the Conversation

foundations-of-trauma-therapy.title: Foundations of Trauma Therapy | Training with Dr. Niki Serravalle | Center for Balanced Living
foundations-of-trauma-therapy.text:
Foundations of Trauma Therapy
Now enrolling: the 12-week Integration Course.
 Founding cohort. Wednesdays, 5:00 to 6:00 PM Eastern, January 13 through April 7, 2027, with no session February 17. Live and virtual. Ten seats. Founding cohort tuition is $395. The founding cohort does not award continuing education credit.
Reserve your seat in the 12-week course
There are at least a dozen recognizable trauma-specific models in circulation. Several are well evidenced. Several are not. All of them are marketed with similar institutional weight, and clinicians develop loyalties that quietly shape treatment decisions. The discipline Foundations teaches is the one that sorts established evidence from emerging evidence from theoretical scaffolding from clinical wisdom, and refuses to collapse them.
The 12-week course
Every clinician trained in a model eventually meets the client for whom it stops working. The course is built around that moment: what tells you the approach has failed, what you do first, how you choose the next move and from which model, and how you know the client is ready to return to the original work. It moves through trauma treatment by model family, one family each week, and integration accumulates across the twelve weeks. One live virtual meeting a week, 60 minutes, capped at ten so the time goes to cases and clinical skill rather than lecture.
Where it started
The September 2026 pilot ran as a two-day intensive. It began with the foundation: the history and ethics of the diagnosis, diagnostic frameworks and differential reasoning across DSM-5-TR and ICD-11, neurobiology taught with explicit attention to what the evidence does and does not license you to say, and assessment and case conceptualization. What that cohort told us shaped the course.
Who this is for
Licensed psychologists, licensed professional counselors, clinical social workers, and associates under supervision.
Presenter
Dr. Niki Serravalle, PsyD, is a licensed clinical psychologist in Delaware. She is EMDRIA Certified, an EMDR Consultant, and an EMDRIA Approved Basic Trainer. She presents EMDR critically in this course, which is the discipline of the material rather than a personal stance.
Reserve your seat in the 12-week course
Later Cohorts
Not ready for January?
The founding cohort of the 12-week course begins January 13, 2027. If the timing does not work for you, add your name and you will hear first when the next cohort opens.

Meet the Author
Niki Serravalle
Dr. Niki Serravalle is a licensed clinical psychologist, author, and the founder of the Center for Balanced Living. Her clinical work centers on trauma-informed care, psychological evaluation, and the integration of nature-based and somatic approaches into therapeutic practice. She writes MUSA from her practice in Delaware, where the clinical and the personal continually meet. Her first book, The Stories We Told: The Dance Between a Codependent and a Compulsive Liar, is forthcoming.
Why I Write
In Latin and Italian, Musa is the muse, the figure who animates writing, thinking, and creative work. To write in the company of a muse was to listen carefully and give shape to what mattered most. It was writing with intention. MUSA is where I house my writing, a space where the clinical, the literary, and the personal meet on the page.
Niki Serravalle
The Book
The Stories We Told
The Dance Between a Codependent and a Compulsive Liar
The Stories We Told is the memoir of a clinical psychologist who knew the signs and stayed anyway, a reckoning with love, deception, and the long work of coming home to herself.

nature-based-emdr-ethical-clinically-gro.title: Nature-Informed EMDR Workshop | 3 EMDRIA Credits | Center for Balanced Living
nature-based-emdr-ethical-clinically-gro.text:
Nature-Informed EMDR: Ethical, Clinically Grounded
Applications
A live, three-hour continuing education workshop for EMDR clinicians who want to think carefully about
when
and
how
nature-informed elements belong inside a standard EMDR case. This is not a new protocol. The eight-phase, three-pronged structure does not change.
The workshop examines how environmental context, sensory grounding, and ecologically attuned elements can serve as adjunctive supports during preparation, affect regulation, and integration. Three modalities are addressed: brought-in natural objects, virtual or
representational nature contact, and in-person outdoor or window-mediated work. Contraindications, accessibility, and clinical decision-making are treated as central, not as an afterthought.
Date & time:
Friday, October 2, 2026, 2:00 to 5:00 PM Eastern
Registration is closed.
Format:
Live webinar via Zoom (real-time, interactive)
Continuing education:
This program has been approved for
3 EMDRIA Credits
Tuition:
$99
Prerequisite:
Completion of an EMDRIA-Approved Basic EMDR Training
What you'll be able to do:
Describe how environmental context influences affect regulation, grounding, and treatment readiness in EMDR
Differentiate standard EMDR procedures from adjunctive nature-informed elements
Identify clinical factors including dissociation risk, accessibility, privacy, and environmental unpredictability
Apply nature-informed strategies to EMDR preparation and integration
Evaluate when a nature-informed element is indicated, contraindicated, or outside the scope of standard EMDR
Presenter:
Niki Serravalle, PsyD, LPCMH, NCC, is a licensed clinical psychologist, EMDRIA Certified Therapist, and EMDRIA Approved Consultant. She is the founder of Center for Balanced Living and CFBL Institute.
This program has been approved for 3 EMDRIA Credits. CFBL Institute maintains responsibility for this program and its content in accordance with EMDRIA requirements. Full EMDR training required. The program site is ADA compliant; contact drserravalle@gmail.com for accommodations. There is no commercial support for this program.

Meet the Author
Dr. Niki Serravalle is a licensed psychologist and licensed professional counselor of mental health, and the founder of Center for Balanced Living in Townsend, Delaware. Her work today centers on psychological evaluation, clinical supervision, consultation, and the training of other clinicians, built on more than two decades of clinical experience.
She began her career at Sheppard Pratt, where she first trained in Dialectical Behavior Therapy and trauma-focused treatment. From there she worked in substance use treatment, intensive outpatient programs for children and adolescents, and community mental health across Maryland and Delaware. Along the way she completed advanced training in EMDR, Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Internal Family Systems, Cognitive Processing Therapy, and ecotherapy.
Her doctorate in clinical psychology turned that foundation toward assessment. Practicum, internship, and postdoctoral training under specialists in neuropsychology and school psychology gave her a lasting focus on diagnostic clarity, and on how neurodevelopment and a person’s environment together shape what a clinician sees.
Through CFBL Institute, she trains and consults with clinicians who want depth rather than a certificate. She is also the author of 
The Stories We Told: The Dance Between a Codependent and a Compulsive Liar
, a memoir published November 12, 2026.
Dr. Serravalle is not currently accepting new individual therapy clients. If you are looking for therapy, the clinical team at Center for Balanced Living is glad to talk with you about fit and availability.

Foundations of Trauma Therapy: 12-Week Integration Course
Wednesdays, 5:00 to 6:00 PM Eastern, through April 7 (no session February 17) · Live on Zoom · Ten seats
Every clinician trained in a model eventually meets the client for whom it stops working. This course is built around that moment: what tells you the approach has failed, what you do first, how you choose the next move and from which model, and how you know the client is ready to return to the original work.

Differential Diagnosis: ADHD, Anxiety, and Trauma
1:00 to 4:00 PM Eastern · Live on Zoom · Ten seats
A substantial portion of what arrives for ADHD evaluation is not ADHD. Sleep, trauma-related attentional disruption, anxiety, mood, learning, and autism all elevate the same rating scales. This intensive works through the reasoning rather than the checklist, taught by a psychologist who administers, scores, and interprets the instruments.
Does not award continuing education credit.
$99

Assessment With Gender-Diverse Clients and Current Trends

How we teach
Every claim, sorted by its evidence
Trauma treatment is crowded with models that arrive with the same confidence and very different support. Every CFBL Institute training sorts what it teaches into four tiers, and each tier licenses a different strength of statement. You leave knowing what you know, and how well.
1
Established
Replicated findings you can state plainly to a client or a colleague.
2
Emerging
Promising evidence still accumulating. Stated with its limits attached.
3
Theoretical
Useful frameworks whose proposed mechanisms have not been tested.
4
Clinical wisdom
What experienced clinicians observe that research has not tested yet. Often right. Not yet proven.
See it in practice

Learn With Dr. Serravalle
Dr. Niki Serravalle brings more than two decades of clinical experience to her teaching, with a focus on helping clinicians and community learners move beyond surface-level information into deeper understanding, clearer conceptualization, and more grounded practice. 
Through CFBL Institute courses and Center for Balanced Living workshops, her trainings are designed to be clinically thoughtful, accessible, and applicable to real work with real people.

the-stories-we-told.text:
MUSA BOOKS
It’s finally time to tell the whole story.
Virtual Launch Party
Thursday, November 12, 7 p.m. Eastern, on Zoom
Come cozy. Pajamas, a mug of cocoa, and stories.
A reading that isn’t in the book.
Once, live. No recording.
At seven, mugs up.
We buy the book together, at a special price.
Questions, then giveaways.
No purchase necessary. Register and attend to be entered.
VIP · 6:30 p.m.
The first guests to register get a private half hour with Niki.
Save your seat.
Registration is free.
The Book
The Stories We Told
The Dance Between a Codependent and a Compulsive Liar
The Stories We Told is the memoir of a clinical psychologist who knew the signs and stayed anyway.
Dr. Niki Serravalle had built a life she was proud of, a practice, three daughters, a hard-won steadiness, when she fell for Ed. He was charm and chaos, fire and ice, a man who could make an ordinary table feel like the center of the world. On their second date she asked him to draw where he saw his life in five years. He sketched a small house on the back of a receipt. She kept it.
What followed was nine years of loving a compulsive liar, and of slowly learning how much of herself she would abandon to keep the story going. This is not a book about a villain. It is a book about the dance. Two people who learned early that love came with conditions, finding a familiar charge in each other. The pull that felt like home. The cost of staying. And the long, unglamorous work of coming back to herself.
Written with the intimacy of memoir and the eye of a psychologist who could not think her way out of it, this is for every woman who has loved someone confusing, stayed longer than she should have, and wondered why. It is her story. Somehow, it is also yours.
PRE-ORDER NOW
An excerpt
Our second date stays vivid in my memory. We both dressed up a little more than the occasion required, because we wanted to impress. We were caught up in candlelight, the slow burn of chemistry thick in the air.
He leaned in across the table, playful and curious. 
So,
 he said with a grin, 
you're going to be a psychologist? Does that mean you can read minds? Or tell the future or something?
I smiled and said, 
Of course I can.
 Then I added, 
Actually, let me show you. Draw me a picture of where you think your life will be in five years.
He laughed, surprised, but his eyes lit up. He dug around, pulled an old receipt from his pocket, and even ran out to his truck to find a pen. Right there on the back of that crumpled slip, he sketched a small house. Simple. Nestled in the woods.
When he handed it back to me, something stirred inside me. 
This tells me everything I need to know about you, Ed,
 I told him softly.
He raised an eyebrow, grinning. 
Really? You got all that from a little picture?
I laughed. 
It's the story of you,
 I said.
Most of all, I saw that he wanted home. Comfort. To belong. A place to have a family.
In that moment, I believed we wanted the same thing.
From Phoenix Rising with Dr. Z, Episode 73

Latest Podcast Episode
What happens when someone dies and, in the process of grieving them, you discover that parts of the person you knew may not have been true?
In Part 1 of this deeply personal conversation, Dr. Christina Zampitella is joined by psychologist and author Dr. Niki Serravalle to explore a complicated and rarely discussed kind of grief: grieving the death of someone who lied about significant parts of their life.
Dr. Serravalle shares the story of her relationship with her late ex-husband, from the intense connection they experienced early on to the small, seemingly inconsequential lies that eventually gave way to much larger deceptions.
Together, Christina and Niki explore the confusion of loving and trusting someone while also learning to overlook inconsistencies, and how patterns of codependency can become intertwined with relationships marked by instability and deception.
The conversation also examines the difference between compulsive lying and intentional manipulation, how codependency can show up even in people who appear strong and self-aware, and the grief that can happen long before a physical death when a relationship or the life you believed you had begins to disappear.
Then, after her late ex-husband’s unexpected death, Niki made a discovery that challenged one of the most fundamental stories he had told about himself. Despite years of describing himself as a Marine and appearing to live with the physical and psychological effects of military service, his family told her he had never served in the military.
That discovery opened an entirely new layer of grief and an unsettling question:
Who exactly are you grieving when you can no longer be certain who the person was?
Part 2 continues 9/15. 
Episode 2
How do you grieve someone when their death leaves you with more questions than answers? 
In Part 2 of this deeply personal conversation, Dr. Christina Zampitella and psychologist and author Dr. Niki Serravalle continue exploring the complicated grief that followed the unexpected death of Niki's ex-husband, Ed. 
After Ed died from a drug overdose, Niki began learning things about his life that didn't fit the person she had known for nine years. She discovered an arrest she knew nothing about, questioned whether drug use had been happening without her knowledge, and began hearing from others who had their own experiences with his lies. 
At the same time, those discoveries didn't erase the person she knew and loved. 
Niki reflects on the challenge of holding those realities together: Ed could lie and still be deeply loved. Their relationship could be chaotic and painful while also containing genuine connection and beautiful memories. She could love him while recognizing that being in a relationship with him was not healthy for her. 
Christina and Niki also explore the unanswered "what ifs" that often accompany grief, the stigma surrounding deaths from drug overdose, and the difference between loving someone and allowing them unrestricted access to your life. 
Niki shares how Ed's death ultimately became part of a much larger journey toward understanding herself, her codependency, her boundaries, and the stories she had carried about who she was.
